Class OnixCommandBase

Namespace
OnixRuntime.Api.OnixClient.Commands
Assembly
OnixRuntime.dll

The base class for all commands. You should inherit from this class to create your own commands. You should mark overload methods with the OnixCommandBase.OverloadAttribute attribute for them to be called.

Execute(OnixCommandOrigin, string)

What actually runs the command. You should NOT override this unless you have a very good reason to. This will handle parsing the parameters and calling the correct overload. If you do override this, you probably also will need to override GetOverloads(). You should declare a function that does what you want and mark it with OnixCommandBase.OverloadAttribute.

public virtual OnixCommandOutput Execute(OnixCommandOrigin origin, string parameters)

GetOverloads()

This is the function that gathers all overloads for this command using reflection. You could technically implement your own but unless you have a good reason to and know what you're doing, don't. You will also need to implement Execute(OnixCommandOrigin, string) if you do replace this.
